$comment: Provenance record for the fixed thresholds baked into scripts/score.py.
These values are CONSTANTS -- score.py does not read this file, does not read
any comparison library, and needs neither present to run. This file exists so
a threshold can be traced back to a measurement instead of asserted on vibes;
it is documentation of how the numbers were chosen during development, not a
runtime dependency. Library names have been generalised to A/B/C -- what
matters is the shape of the evidence, not which specific files produced it.
Anyone can reproduce or update this calibration against their own set with:
harness: measure.py, morphological-close coverage (R=2), outermost-container row gaps
sample_size: 3 professionally produced carousel template libraries, 40-250 cards each, none creator-built

observed_range.note: Auto-detection found 250 artboard-shaped elements in this file; low coverage likely reflects a genuinely minimal system plus some detection noise. Treated as a weak, low-confidence data point.

coverage_floor.basis: Observed sample mean coverage was 0.68-0.69 for two of the three libraries. A 0.40 per-card floor sits comfortably under both, so it rejects genuinely sparse cards without penalising well-composed work. Before a morphological-close fix to the coverage measurement, this floor was unreachable by every library in the sample -- which is how that measurement bug was originally found.

coverage_ceiling.basis: An initial 0.78 ceiling flagged 22-28% of sample cards as overpacked -- a threshold failing, not a finding: a full-bleed photograph is 100% covered by design. Two corrections: raised to 0.88, and restricted to text-only cards. A card that is all text and still near-total coverage is the actual failure mode this threshold targets.

gap_cv.basis: The tightest library in the sample measured 0.32 gap coefficient-of-variation. Set at the best-observed value rather than the sample mean: the gate should reward matching the best available work, not the average of it.

distinct_font_sizes.basis: Sample libraries ran 43-68 distinct computed font sizes -- none locked a type ramp. A library holding under 22 already beats every library in the sample on this axis; under 11 means a nine-step ramp plus a figure ramp is genuinely being obeyed.

slack_free.basis: Sample median bottom slack was 60-76px. 160 leaves normal composition unflagged and catches only real holes.

row_gap_ceiling.basis: Rhythm-relative rather than absolute so it survives a change of artboard or type scale.

known_limits: Coverage is a 40x50 raster approximation of union area, not exact geometry. Stable across runs and slightly generous, which keeps it from becoming a nuisance metric.

Foreign libraries (no project manifest) are measured in degraded mode: artboard auto-detected, no intent licensing, distinction capped at 60%. Every degraded reading is scored in the foreign library's favour.
Webfont availability shifts text metrics. measure.py reports document.fonts.status; compare only runs with the same font state.
The 250-card sample's count is unverified and may include non-artboard elements of the same width -- treated as low-confidence throughout.

This sample is small (n=3). The thresholds are reasonable starting points, not statistically robust bounds. Re-running /design-system-carousel-creator:bench against a larger or different sample and updating this file is expected as the tool sees more use.
